title: Private Deploy DR Runbook + Terraform module notes and Upgrade checklist
content:
Purpose:
This runbook captures proposed disaster recovery (DR) procedures, backup and restore patterns, Terraform module considerations, and an upgrade checklist for Redwood private deployments (VPC & on-prem). It is intended for SREs, infra engineers, and customer onboarding engineers preparing production private deployments and performing DR drills.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to Private deployments managed by Redwood’s control plane with customer-managed network and storage (VPC and on-prem variants).
- Covers critical state: Postgres metadata DB, model artifact storage (S3-compatible), runtime node configs, Kubernetes manifests (if used), Terraform state/backends, and KV caches that must be rebuilt.
- Targets assume at least one cross-region/secondary backup target for hosted object storage and a remote Terraform state backend with locking.

Recovery objectives (recommended defaults):
- RTO (time to recovery): 1–4 hours for customer-facing inference endpoints (depending on SLA tier).
- RPO (data loss tolerance): 15 minutes for metadata changes; 24 hours for large artifact syncs if bandwidth-constrained.

Inventory of critical artifacts to backup:
1) PostgreSQL logical dumps (schema + latest WAL segments) and periodic base backups
2) Object store: model artifacts, config blobs, logs snapshot index (S3/MinIO buckets)
3) Terraform remote state files + lock metadata (state per environment)
4) Kubernetes manifests/Helm release values (if on-prem K8s) stored in git and as tarball backups
5) Secrets (KMS-wrapped or HSM references) — ensure separate export path per compliance policy
6) Certificate/key material and ingress controller configs
7) KV caches and ephemeral caches (note: intentionally rebuildable; not required in backups but capture bootstrap params)

Backup strategy (patterns):
- Database:
  - Daily base backups with hourly WAL shipping to remote object storage. Use pg_basebackup for full periodic checkpoints and wal-e/wal-g or built-in managed replication to push WALs.
  - Retention policy: keep daily for 14 days, weekly for 90 days, monthly for 12 months (tune per customer).

- Object storage (models, artifacts):
  - Use lifecycle rules to snapshot manifest indexes daily. For large models, keep incremental manifests referencing immutable content-addressed blobs.
  - Cross-region/object-replicas (if possible) for critical artifacts. If using on-prem MinIO, enable bucket replication to an offsite S3 endpoint.

- Terraform state:
  - Remote backend (S3/GCS/Consul/ArgoCD) mandatory. Enable server-side encryption, object versioning, and state locking (DynamoDB or Consul).
  - Periodic export: scheduled job to copy state files to a dedicated DR bucket with timestamped filenames.

- Kubernetes manifests / helm values:
  - Keep repo as canonical source; in addition, push periodic tarball snapshots of active manifests to object store. Tag snapshots with cluster-id + timestamp.

- Secrets:
  - Do NOT keep plaintext in object storage. Export encrypted KMS/HSM snapshots where policy allows; store recovery procedure referencing KMS account recovery.

Terraform module notes (practical changes & gotchas):
- Module design: split stateful resources into their own module/state (postgres, objectstore, network) and stateless infra (apps, autoscaler) in separate states to reduce blast radius during partial restores.
- State locking: ensure locking is configured consistently across environments. Missing locks is the highest cause of accidental drift during restores.
- Drift detection: automated periodic plan runs saved as artifacts. Keep a last-known-good plan in the DR bucket to speed verification after restore.
- Secrets in TF: avoid storing plaintext secrets in tfstate by using data sources that reference external secret stores (Vault/KMS).
- Idempotency: modules should allow re-apply of init/bootstrap without destructive deletion; use resource lifecycle prevent_destroy where needed for recoverable components.
- Provider versions: pin providers per module and archive provider plugins in an internal registry to avoid upgrade-time surprises during DR restores.

Restore playbook (high-level, step-by-step):
1) Incident declaration and scope: confirm impacted systems and desired recovery target (full site, region, model set). Notify communications channel and paging list.
2) Identify last-good backup timestamps for DB and artifacts.
3) Provision base infra (network + terraform state restore):
   - If primary state is lost, retrieve most recent state copy from DR bucket. Restore remote backend object and re-establish lock with a controlled temporary lock-holder.
   - Apply terraform modules for networking and persistent volumes in "plan-only" mode first, validate resources created.
4) Restore Object Storage:
   - Create buckets and enable versioning and lifecycle. Restore model artifacts from the latest snapshot/replica. Verify checksums for critical models.
5) Restore DB:
   - Initialize a clean postgres instance, restore base backup, then apply WAL replay up to target_time. Start in single-user mode and verify schema consistency.
6) Deploy control-plane services (auth, routing, ingress) with manifests from snapshot. Start in maintenance mode.
7) Bring up runtime nodes and workers. Rehydrate caches via warmup jobs that replay recent inference requests from logs (if available) or via synthetic traffic.
8) Smoke tests and validation (see test checklist). If all pass, cut traffic and monitor closely for error rates and latency degradation.
9) Post-restore: rotate keys/certificates if compromise suspected. Conduct a postmortem and update runbook.

Validation checks (smoke tests):
- API readiness probes across control-plane endpoints
- Sample inference end-to-end against a small stable model artifact
- DB integrity checks (counts of expected rows, basic FK checks)
- Artifact checksum verification for top 10 models by size
- Terraform state consistency check (terraform plan against restored backend expected to be no-op for infra)

Rollback and rollback-prevention tips:
- Take immutable snapshots before any destructive step (e.g., before force-unlocking terraform state).
- Tag each manual intervention with the ticket/incident id and operator username.
- When rolling back an upgrade, prefer to restore infra and artifacts from snapshot rather than attempt reverse schema migrations in-place unless fully tested.

Upgrade plan integration with DR:
- Pre-upgrade: take full DB + artifact snapshot and export terraform state; run a dry-run of the upgrade in a staging DR cluster using the same upgrade artifacts.
- Canary: upgrade a single non-critical node/zone; run smoke tests and monitor metrics and error budgets.
- Cutover policy: automatic rollback window of 30 minutes if error-rate or latency breaches thresholds.
- Post-upgrade: keep old artifacts retained for 7 days and have an explicit retention-fast path for urgent rollbacks.

DR drills and frequency:
- Quarterly tabletop exercises with engineering + support + customer success for high-SLA customers.
- Full restore drill of a non-prod clone at least twice per year.
- Partial restores (single model artifact, single DB schema subset) monthly for exercise.

Communication and runbook ownership:
- DR owner: eng-sre on-call lead for the cluster during incident.
- Communication channels: #private-dr-alerts Slack (incident), status.redwood.ai for public notices, and a dedicated incident Zoom bridge.
- Post-incident: the runbook owner creates an incident summary doc and links to the PR that updates Terraform modules or backup config.

Appendix: quick command snippets (examples)
- Export terraform state snapshot:
  aws s3 cp s3://tfstate-prod/private-deployments/terraform.tfstate s3://dr-archive/tfstate-prod-$(date +%Y%m%dT%H%M).tfstate 

- Postgres base backup (example):
  pg_basebackup -h primary-db -D /var/lib/postgresql/backup -U replicator -Ft -z -P

- Restore object artifacts (MinIO -> S3):
  mc cp --recursive myminio/models/ s3/dr-archive/models/ --overwrite 

Open questions / action items (to resolve):
- Decide final RPO for premium customers (15 mins vs 5 mins) and impact on WAL shipping costs.
- Confirm offsite replication target for customers without cloud accounts (partner-managed cold site?).
- Add a signed-off checklist for KMS/HSM recovery from customer security teams.

Next steps:
- Run a dry-run restore of the smallest customer private deployment in staging (assigned: Diego). Deadline: 2025-02-15.
- Update Terraform modules to split stateful resources (assigned: Linnea). Deadline: 2025-03-01.
- Draft customer-facing DR one-pager with RTO/RPO options for onboarding (assigned: Aisha). Deadline: 2025-02-28.

Revision history:
- 2025-01-10: initial draft (Aisha Patel)
- 2025-01-22: added terraform module recommendations (Linnea Wong)
